guides.title: When is Saint Demetrios name day?
guides.seo_title: When is Saint Demetrios name day? Dimitris, Dimitrios and Dimitra
guides.desc: Saint Demetrios name day is October 26 (November 8 on the Old Calendar). Who celebrates it, what to say, and the KRIOS film on the feast.
guides.lead: October 26. On the calendar followed by the Church of Greece, the feast of Saint Demetrios (Άγιος Δημήτριος), the saint of Thessaloniki, falls on October 26 every year.

p: People named Dimitris (Δημήτρης), Dimitrios (Δημήτριος) and Dimitra (Δήμητρα) celebrate their name day on the feast of Saint Demetrios.
Churches that keep the Old (Julian) Calendar celebrate the same feast 13 days later, on November 8 of the civil calendar.
The usual wish on a name day is Χρόνια πολλά (Chronia polla), “many years”.

guides.title: Ohi Day, October 28
guides.seo_title: Ohi Day, October 28: what happened in 1940 and how Greeks remember it
guides.desc: Why Greeks mark October 28: Italy's ultimatum of 1940, the refusal that became the word ΟΧΙ, and how the day is remembered in Greece and abroad.
guides.lead: On October 28, Greeks remember the morning in 1940 when Greece refused Italy's ultimatum and went to war. It is a national holiday in Greece and in Cyprus.

p: Just before three in the morning, the Italian ambassador, Emanuele Grazzi, arrived at the house of Prime Minister Ioannis Metaxas in Kifissia, near Athens. He carried an ultimatum from Mussolini: let Italian troops into Greece to occupy strategic points.
Metaxas did not answer with a single word. Speaking French, he told the ambassador that this meant war. The Greek people turned that refusal into one word: ΟΧΙ, “no”.
At half past five, before the deadline had even expired, Italian troops crossed from Albania into Epirus.

The refusal came from Metaxas, who had ruled Greece as a dictator since 1936. The resistance that followed belonged to the whole nation. In the mountains of the Pindus, where mules could not climb, women carried shells and supplies on their own backs.
Greeks marked the anniversary even under occupation, and after liberation it became a national holiday.
In Thessaloniki, soldiers march before the President of the Republic. In towns and villages across Greece, schoolchildren parade under blue-and-white flags.
On the same day the Church of Greece celebrates the Protection of the Theotokos (Αγία Σκέπη), a feast it placed on October 28 in 1952. It is a church feast, separate from the national commemoration.
Abroad, Greek communities gather in church and at war memorials. In Australia, doxologies and wreath-layings are held in Melbourne, Sydney and Adelaide.
